entries.test: Public evaluations of historically dominant neural network architectures on tasks outside their training distributions would establish their generalization difficulties.
entries.note: The architectural qualification matters; this is not a claim about every possible neural network.

entries.test: Controlled evaluations comparing reasoning and planning within and beyond training distributions would test whether generalization limitations reduce reliability.
entries.note: The normalization omits the inherited restriction to configurations dominant over the preceding three decades.

entries.test: Public scaling experiments and documented developer data-acquisition decisions would test whether generalization limitations drive data requirements and ethically consequential practices.
entries.note: The normalization drops the architectural qualification and broadens past developer choices into a general claim. Observable practices and documented decisions can supply evidence without inferring private motives.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of whether increasing training data eliminates failures on previously unseen cases would test the claim that outliers necessarily remain.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies the meaning of 'enough data.' An indefinite horizon does not itself make the claim uncheckable.

entries.test: Public driverless-service deployment records as of publication and technical evidence about deployment limitations would test both the 'just demos' premise and its proposed cause.
entries.note: 'Still just demos' has a factual reading about operational deployment despite its dismissive wording.

entries.test: Independent evaluations and deployment records demonstrating sustained reliable LLM reasoning and planning on unfamiliar cases would challenge the permanent unreliability prediction.
entries.note: 'Inability to generalize' strengthens 'trouble generalizing'; Marcus explicitly allows some generalization. The forecast also includes a causal explanation.

entries.test: Public scaling experiments measuring performance gains from successive increases in training data would establish whether marginal returns diminish.
entries.note: 'What we can expect' expresses a firm expectation here. The surrounding discussion identifies data scaling as its subject.

entries.test: Public evaluations of models available at publication would test whether they generalize somewhat while failing reliable reasoning and planning beyond their training distributions.
entries.note: The surrounding text supplies a practical reading of 'not enough': insufficient generalization for reliable reasoning and planning.

entries.test: Public estimates of training-data requirements and available usable data would establish whether exponentially growing requirements exceed supply.
A publicly demonstrated AGI achieved by scaling existing approaches without improved beyond-training generalization would falsify the asserted requirement.
entries.note: This asserts a technical necessity for achieving AGI, rather than a value judgment about what researchers ought to pursue.
